ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, charter counterparties, vessel owners, and escrow agents against the Egyptian AML/CFT Unit domestic terrorist list (Law No. 94/2015), the Central Bank of Egypt sanctions circulars, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Resolution 1267/1988/1989 and 1267 ISIL/AL-Qaida consolidated list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and national commercial registry disqualification databases. Enhanced Due Diligence is required for all PEPs and for offshore marine charter counterparties, with mandatory disclosure of any PEP relationship, vessel beneficial ownership chain, flag registry, and source of charter hire funds prior to incorporation approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI e-Investment Portal ('Invest in Egypt' One-Stop-Shop) and the Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade – integrated via the Egypt.gov.eg digital services gateway
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name shall be registered in Arabic as the statutory and mandatory language. Foreign-language names must be accompanied by an official phonetic Arabic transliteration approved by a certified translator and accepted by the GAFI One-Stop-Shop and the Commercial Registry. The Arabic commercial name must not conflict with any prior registered trademark or existing commercial registration. The Latin-script name is accepted for foreign trade identification but does not supersede the binding Arabic name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Islamic (requires ministerial authorization from the competent religious authority)
Words implying state sponsorship or public utility concessions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name clearance is sought at GAFI One-Stop-Shop before incorporation filing. Rejected names receive a written refusal with grounds. The applicant may file a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Registration Committee within 15 working days of rejection, attaching the Arabic transliteration certificate and trademark search results. If the Committee denies the appeal, the applicant may resubmit a new name without resubmission fee. Judicial remedy is available before the State Council (Administrative Court) within 60 days of the final administrative decision. A general reservation extension of 30 days may be requested only within the validity window, before expiry, if the incorporation file is already in process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable for this industry. Offshore marine charter licensing requires a physical registered office in Egypt with a permanently staffed desk, Arabic-language correspondence capability, and accessible corporate records. Virtual or pure mail-forwarding offices are rejected by GAFI and the Maritime Transport Sector. A serviced office with dedicated physical workspace, board meeting capacity, appointment of an Egyptian correspondent, and documented substance commitment is acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45 percent likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection within 24 months of incorporation, triggered by the GAFI anti-money-laundering supervision cycle, AML/CFT Unit targeted maritime-sector examinations, and Egyptian Maritime Transport Sector operational audits. Vessel leasing activity also increases the probability of coordinated inspections with port authority officials.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law) as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009, Articles 102–152 (Limited Liability Companies); complemented by Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 for GAFI one-stop-shop administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Incorporation Contract) and Electronic GAFI Incorporation Application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For LLCs, minimum subscribed capital is EGP 50,000 divided into shares of not less than EGP 100 each; no mandatory upfront escrow deposit, but the shareholders must fund capital within five years. For offshore vessel charter, GAFI may require evidence of capital adequacy aligned with vessel acquisition or bareboat charter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED BY THE Board of Shareholders of [Company Name] LLC at its constituent meeting held this day: (1) that each shareholder's subscription to the share capital be accepted in the amounts set forth in the Articles of Association, and that the Shareholders' Representative be authorized to open a bank account and deposit the initial paid-up contributions; (2) that the registered office of the company is hereby established at the address specified in the Articles of Association; (3) that Mr. [Name] be appointed as General Manager and Mrs. [Name] as Company Secretary, both with full authority to execute and file all statutory applications before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, tax authorities, and maritime licensing bodies; (4) that the company seal, corporate books, and maritime operation records be procured immediately. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Status Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request through the GAFI e-service portal, providing three alternative names and the proposed company legal form (LLC). Payment of the prescribed fee is made electronically. After approval, obtain the name reservation certificate valid for sixty (60) days.
required_dossiers: Copy of national ID or passport for all shareholders
Declaration of lawful object (offshore supply vessel leasing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a written clarification demonstrating distinctiveness; reapply with revised alternatives within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Office at the GAFI one-stop-shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association reflecting the shareholders' agreement, capital subscription, management structure, and registered office. Appear before the Notary Public with all shareholders and legal representatives. The notary will certify signatures and officialize the incorporation contract.
required_dossiers: Indicative bank certificate showing payment of incorporation fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises formal deficiencies, correct the Articles and renotarize within five days; expedited service available for urgent commercial filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration at the Egyptian Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Department, Ministry of Trade and Industry (via GAFI window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Association and incorporation application to the Commercial Registry through the GAFI one-stop-shop. The registry will issue the Commercial Registration Certificate, which constitutes the formal existence of the LLC as a legal entity.
required_dossiers: Copy of lease contract or proof of registered office address
Valid national IDs of shareholders and managers
Tax ID form for the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the file, rectify missing signatures or address documentation within seven days; request a formal corrective notice from GAFI to re-file without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, apply for a tax card at the ETA office serving the registered address and simultaneously register the company and its employees with the social insurance authority. Obtain the tax identification number and social insurance certificate.
required_dossiers: National IDs and employment declarations for officers and workers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to incomplete employee data, file a correction within ten days; pay any late-fee assessments only after verifying the initial registration date with GAFI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of GAFI Investment License and Final Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of steps 1–4, GAFI reviews the integrated file and issues the Investment License and a consolidated Incorporation Certificate for the LLC. This license authorizes the company to undertake commercial and maritime charter operations and to open an import/export file.
required_dossiers: Certified bank capital deposit or confirmation
GAFI application forms and fee receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a notice of deficiency, respond with additional proof of capital or statutory documents within fifteen days; an administrative review resort is available under Law No. 72 of 2017.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime Operating License and Vessel Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Maritime Transport (GAMT) – Maritime Safety Administration; Egyptian Maritime Data Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company incorporation documents to GAMT to obtain an Offshore Supply Vessel Operation Permit. For each vessel, submit technical specifications, classification certificates, insurance coverage, and crew qualifications; the vessel will be registered in the Egyptian registry or approved under a temporary license for offshore supply activities in Egyptian waters.
required_dossiers: Vessel ownership title or notarized bareboat charter agreement
Original vessel classification certificate (e.g., IACS class)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the maritime safety inspection identifies defects, rectify deficiencies in the vessel's equipment or documentation within twenty days and request reinspection; appeal any denial to the GAMT Review Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment and Operating Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) category inclusion request to EEAA for the offshore vessel chartering and port-based operations. For activities involving vessel anchorages, bunkering, and wastewater discharge, prepare a full EIA report in consultation with an approved environmental advisor. Receive the environmental management plan approval prior to commencement of operations.
required_dossiers: Technical vessel specifications including emissions and waste stream data
Marine pollution prevention plan (MARPOL compliance evidence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If EEAA requires additional baseline data, submit supplementary environmental sampling and modeling within thirty days; or request a resubmission meeting to resolve scoping disputes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Maritime Transport (GAMT) – Offshore Services Licensing Directorate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) under Law No. 4 of 1994 and its amendments
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) required for offshore platform support vessel operations and associated coastal shore facilities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL 73/78 Annex I (oil discharge threshold ≤ 15 ppm for treated bilge water), Annex IV (sewage treatment), Annex V (garbage management) and Annex VI (NOx/SOx and VOC emissions); Egyptian Prime-Degrees impose zero-discharge from coastal junctures and mandatory shore-reception facility usage for slop and sludge.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Egyptian Civil Defense Authority for onshore offices, fuel storage areas, and mooring installations; structural load inspection certificate for jetties or quay facilities; occupational safety clearance from the Ministry of Manpower and Migration covering worker training, lifebuoy and life-raft provisioning, and emergency preparedness drills.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — central tax administration operating the unified e-Tax portal (eta.gov.eg) and the ETA e-Invoicing/e-Receipt clearance platforms
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must apply for a unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and tax card through the ETA e-Tax portal using the unified tax registration workflow. Required filings include the certificate of incorporation and memorandum/Articles of Association, Commercial Registry extract, corporate board resolution, notarized legalized power of attorney in favor of the local fiscal representative, and identification documents of directors/shareholders. A foreign entity without a fixed Egyptian establishment that supplies taxable services into Egypt must separately appoint an Egyptian fiscal representative and register for VAT under Law No. 67/2016; the ETA issues a single TIN that integrates income tax, VAT, and stamp tax registration records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person taxed at entity level on worldwide income under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005; shareholders are not pass-through participants; no US-style check-the-box regime exists
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available. Permitted elections and administrative mechanisms include: (i) adopting an ETA-approved non-calendar fiscal year; (ii) filing consolidated corporate tax returns for a qualifying Egyptian group subject to prior ETA approval (Law No. 91/2005); (iii) tax depreciation method and rate elections; and (iv) documentary transfer-pricing compliance elections. Hybrid mismatch arrangements are not recognized under domestic Egyptian tax law, and BEPS-aligned general anti-abuse rules prevail.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Egyptian Law No. 67/2016, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration applies once the annual value of taxable supplies exceeds EGP 500,000; voluntary registration is available below the threshold; non-resident suppliers with Egyptian VAT nexus must register through an Egyptian fiscal representative
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The ETA mandates real-time electronic invoicing (e-Invoice) and electronic receipt (e-Receipt) reporting. Taxable persons must submit structured XML or JSON invoices to the ETA platform via approved APIs or web portal, digitally sign/stamp invoices with an ETA-accredited e-signature, and obtain automatic validation and fiscal clearance before use. B2C transactions must use machine-readable e-Receipts. Non-compliance triggers disconnection of e-signature clearance, refusal of invoice ratification, and statutory penalties under Law No. 67/2016 and the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 188/2020.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) tangible goods physically exported from Egypt within the statutory timeframe and evidenced by ETA and Customs-approved export declarations, and (ii) services supplied to non-resident persons and wholly or effectively consumed outside Egypt, including international transport and maritime services ancillary thereto. Offshore platform vessel leasing/chartering to non-resident operators qualifies when the lease is with a non-resident charterer, the vessel operates in international waters beyond Egyptian territorial waters or supports offshore installations outside the Egyptian VAT territory, and consideration is paid in foreign currency through the Egyptian banking system. The taxpayer must issue the export invoice through the ETA e-Invoice platform with the statutory export code, present the underlying charter contract, and submit customs and banking evidence; input VAT connected to zero-rated export sales is refundable after ETA verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document lodged through the NAFEZA single window) duly stamped by Egyptian Customs and ETA
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill evidencing exportation of goods and/or vessel dispatch to non-Egyptian offshore points
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorized Egyptian bank confirming receipt of foreign currency from the non-resident charterer
ETA-cleared XML e-Invoice carrying the zero-rated export code and digital fiscal stamp
Time charter, voyage charter, or bareboat lease contract and offshore platform supply service order identifying the non-resident customer and the delivery/service location
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to automated ETA cross-checks among the e-Invoice/e-Receipt clearing system, Egyptian Customs NAFEZA records, and Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) foreign-exchange repatriation records. Failure to substantiate physical export or offshore consumption, or failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day CBE deadline, exposes the taxpayer to reassessment of VAT at the standard rate of 14%, late-payment interest and additional tax, administrative fines, criminal monetary penalties and imprisonment for deliberate fraud, suspension from e-Invoice clearance, and retrospective clawback of refunds and zero-rating for the applicable statutory limitation period (up to five years), with joint liability for the local fiscal representative where applicable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - the sole monetary authority and foreign-exchange administration - exercising powers conferred by the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, its Executive Regulations, and the CBE Unified Foreign Exchange Rules binding on all banks and licensed payment service providers in Egypt.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified, market-determined managed float for the Egyptian Pound (EGP) and holds IMF Article VIII status, under which current-account international payments, including offshore charter hire and vessel-leasing fees payable to an Egyptian resident exporter, are fully convertible through CBE-licensed banks without prior central-bank approval. Capital-account inflows by non-resident shareholders are freely admissible at entry under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, but the right to repatriate capital and dividends is compliance-based: the foreign investor must register the inward remittance with the receiving Egyptian bank under the CBE capital-registration mechanism and, at the time of outward remittance, must present audited financial statements, tax clearance, and the bank-issued capital-registration certificate. Following the March 2024 comprehensive FX liberalization, dividend and capital repatriation orders are executable by banks at the prevailing interbank spot rate without prior CBE approval. Residual hurdles are limited to correspondent-bank source-of-funds due diligence and mandatory balance-of-payments reporting by the bank. For this LLC, US-dollar charter income earned from non-resident charterers constitutes an export of services under ISIC 5222 and is freely receivable into an Egyptian foreign-currency retention account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE regulations issued pursuant to Law No. 194 of 2020, export service proceeds, including offshore supply-vessel charter and leasing hire, must be repatriated to Egypt and credited to a CBE-licensed bank account within 180 days from the date the charter service is performed (30 days for physical goods export shipments). The full hard-currency receipt must enter the exporter's Egyptian foreign-currency retention account; the compulsory surrender-conversion ratios in force before March 2024 have been repealed, and exporters may currently retain 100% of receipts in foreign currency for working capital, import settlement, loan servicing, and lawful dividend distribution, provided the bank is notified and the underlying charter contract, hire invoices, and collection evidence are maintained. Non-repatriation, retention of proceeds in an unauthorized offshore account, or false export declarations constitute exchange-control violations under Law No. 194 of 2020, expose the account to freeze, and trigger mandatory disclosure to the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (EFCU) under AML Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2023.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury rail; MEDIUM only as an auxiliary collection-and-payment conduit subject to strict legal constraints. Under Law No. 194 of 2020 and CBE payment-system regulations, only CBE-licensed banks and registered payment service providers may hold or settle EGP balances or access the domestic RTGS (EGNCH) and InstaPay instant-payment rails. Offshore digital EMIs, such as UK FCA-licensed or EU-licensed electronic-money institutions, cannot open EGP IBANs and have no direct access to the Egyptian interbank system. They may lawfully act as multi-currency collection agents vis-a-vis foreign charterers, but every USD/EUR collection must be promptly swept by SWIFT MT103 into the LLC's Egyptian foreign-currency retention account to satisfy the 180-day export-receipts repatriation window. The Egyptian account bank must remain the ultimate settlement institution, and the EMI's transaction data must be fully reconcilable for CBE balance-of-payments statistics and EFCU reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. At least one authorized signatory, being the LLC's duly appointed local manager or the holder of a notarized, apostilled, and Egyptian-consularized power of attorney granted by the non-resident directors, must attend the chosen branch in person to execute the corporate account mandate, specimen signature card, and facility documentation. Fully remote or fully digital onboarding is not available for this foreign-owned offshore chartering entity; video-call identity verification may supplement but cannot replace the in-branch interview. The mandatory KYC/AML file comprises: certificate of incorporation and Commercial Registry extract (السجل التجاري), tax card and tax registration certificate, investment certificate obtained from the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) attesting to foreign ownership, the statutory maritime operating licence issued by the competent Egyptian authority for platform-supply vessel chartering, a certified board resolution naming account signatories, a complete UBO register under AML Law No. 80 of 2002, certified passports and resident permits of all directors and of the attorney-in-fact, and IFRS opening financial statements or audited annual accounts of the LLC and, where relevant, of the foreign parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign parent company resident in a low-tax or non-rated jurisdiction, combined with the Egyptian LLC showing no visible physical office, payroll, or operational substance in Egypt.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation and corporate-register extract of the parent; consolidated IFRS-audited financial statements with unqualified audit opinion; complete UBO organizational chart traced to natural persons with certified passport copies; proof of parent economic substance (office leases, payroll records, physical assets); Egypt-side commercial lease, utility invoices, staffing and payroll records for the LLC; board resolution authorizing the opening of accounts and signatories; Egyptian tax card and Commercial Registry extract; and a written business plan evidencing genuine offshore vessel-chartering activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Maritime-industry red flag: chartering through multiple special-purpose vehicles, perceived 'dark-fleet' or sanctions exposure of vessels, or high-value charter hire from unrelated or newly incorporated counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel IMO and flag-state registration certificates; executed BIMCO-form charter-party contracts with transparent hire-rate formulas; invoices and bank statements matched against voyage schedules; real-time OFAC/EU/UN sanctions-screening reports covering charterers, vessel registered owner, commercial manager, and P&I club; SIRE or OVID inspection certificates; AIS position logs demonstrating physical trading activity; an affidavit explaining the commercial necessity of any multi-SPV collection structure; and bank statements evidencing that all receipts are credited to the Egyptian retention account within the statutory 180-day window.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection in round amounts from a jurisdiction under FATF enhanced monitoring, or shareholder funding sourced from third-party loans and intercompany balances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement and complete capitalization table; source-of-funds dossier comprising the shareholder's audited financial statements, historical bank statements reflecting accumulation of the wired amount, and the executed intercompany loan agreement where applicable; notarized and apostilled corporate resolutions of the lending shareholder; external compliance-counsel source-of-wealth memorandum rating the shareholder's jurisdiction, ownership structure, and legitimacy; correspondent-bank confirmation of the wire chain through reputable institutions such as JPMorgan Chase, Citibank, or BNY Mellon; and the completed CBE capital-registration application filed with the receiving Egyptian bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow_Maritime payment rail perceived as circumventing Egypt's export-proceeds repatriation obligation because funds pause with an offshore marine escrow agent before reaching the Egyptian LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed escrow-agency agreement designating a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank as the account bank of record or final settlement party; SWIFT MT103 evidence demonstrating that every escrow disbursement ultimately credits the LLC's Egyptian foreign-currency retention account; written compliance sign-off from the Egyptian bank confirming that the escrow arrangement does not constitute a prohibited offshore account; monthly reconciliation between the escrow agent's statements and the Egyptian bank statements; delivery/redelivery and off-hire protocols governing conditional release of hire; and a written legal opinion from Egyptian counsel confirming exchange-control and AML compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) the non-resident shareholder initiates a SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for very large values) through its home-country bank and a recognized correspondent such as JPMorgan Chase, Citibank, or Bank of New York Mellon, addressed to the receiving Egyptian bank and designating the LLC's foreign-currency account; the payment narrative must read 'Share capital contribution under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017' and reference the LLC's Commercial Registry number and CBE capital-registration file. (2) The Egyptian bank validates the inbound FDI purpose code 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' (or 'Intercompany Loan' for shareholder loans) and performs source-of-funds verification. (3) The LLC submits the board resolution, subscription agreement, shareholder incorporation documents, and UBO declaration. (4) The bank credits the foreign-currency account under a 'capital under registration' status and thereafter issues the CBE capital-registration certificate, which is the mandatory instrument for any future dividend, interest, or capital repatriation. (5) The LLC separately registers the foreign investment with GAFI to secure statutory investment protection. (6) Verification is completed via the MT103 credit advice, the bank's purpose-code confirmation, and the CBE registration certificate; conversion into EGP, if required for working capital, is executed at the prevailing interbank rate without CBE prior approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (a) international supplier, bunker, insurance, and P&I-club disbursements are executed by SWIFT MT103/MT102 direct credits through the Egyptian bank's correspondent network; (b) imports of vessel components, spare parts, and marine equipment are settled through documentary commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 under UCP600, typically at the trade desks of CIB, NBE, or QNB ALAHLI, with the maritime escrow account available for performance and security deposits; (c) the maritime-specific Escrow_Maritime rail interposes a marine escrow agent between charterer and LLC so that hire and security deposits are released only against signed delivery/redelivery and off-hire protocols, after which settlement is routed by SWIFT MT103 to the LLC's Egyptian retention account; (d) domestic EGP disbursements, including port dues, Suez Canal transit fees, crew salaries, and local supplier payments, settle through Egypt's RTGS (EGNCH) and the InstaPay instant-payment system; (e) mandatory tax and social-insurance payments are executed exclusively in EGP through bank transfers with the relevant treasury reference codes; (f) all foreign-currency conversions on the outbound side are executed at the same-day interbank spot rate, supported by proforma invoices, charter parties, or LC applications retained for CBE balance-of-payments and tax-audit evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP outright forwards executed onshore with CBE-licensed banks, normally up to 12 months tenor, available only against documented underlying charter-hire receivables and renewable beyond 12 months with CBE approval based on submitted exposure evidence.

USD/EGP FX swaps (simultaneous spot and forward legs) used to align temporary mismatches between charter-hire receipts and disbursement dates, priced at the interbank swap points and supported by underlying cash-flow forecasts.

USD/EGP cross-currency interest-rate swaps for medium-term vessel-finance and refinancing exposure, permitted where the Egyptian bank confirms the notional corresponds to actual debt-service and hire-income streams.

USD-call/EGP-put options and zero-cost collar structures executed with CBE-licensed banks to hedge the economic value of forecast charter cash flows, subject to board-approved treasury policy and bank credit limits.

NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) are not permissible onshore; Egyptian-resident entities may not conclude offshore NDFs without prior CBE authorization, and hedging is therefore required to be structured as onshore deliverable forwards or swaps referenced to the official interbank fixing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, auditor report, and ordinary general meeting documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), where filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary general meeting generally within three months after the end of the financial year; filing timing follows applicable GAFI requirements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, filing rejection, regulatory notices, and potential suspension or administrative dissolution for persistent non-compliance; no universal fixed strike-off period applies to all Egyptian LLCs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, normally by 1 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and other sanctions under the Unified Tax Procedures Law; repeated or serious non-compliance may trigger tax assessment, enforcement, and referral for further action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll and withholding tax reconciliations and returns, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Periodic filings generally monthly or quarterly, with annual reconciliation obligations where applicable under the relevant tax regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, interest, tax assessment, collection enforcement, and potential administrative or criminal exposure for material non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social insurance wage and employee data reconciliation, if employees are registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reconciliation timing follows social insurance procedures; monthly contribution payments and employee updates apply during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment additional amounts, contribution assessments, collection measures, and penalties for inaccurate or omitted employee data

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal or confirmation of sectoral maritime, vessel, port, or operating approvals, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Relevant maritime, port, transport, or other sector regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: According to the expiry date and renewal cycle of each license or permit; no single national annual renewal date applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension, non-renewal, administrative fines, vessel or operational restrictions, and possible cancellation of the relevant license

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Egyptian LLC established under the Companies Law is generally required to appoint a qualified external auditor and prepare audited financial statements; no general small-company exemption should be assumed without confirming the entity's regime, size, and GAFI status
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards, substantially aligned with IFRS; IFRS may apply where specifically required or elected under the applicable regulatory regime

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No universal standalone annual UBO confirmation filing should be assumed. The company must maintain accurate beneficial ownership and control information, update it promptly after ownership or control changes, preserve supporting records, and provide the information to competent authorities, financial institutions, or regulators when required. LLC quota transfers require the applicable authenticated transfer documentation and updates to the company and official records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and ownership interests
Register of beneficial owners and controlling persons
Minute book for general meetings and manager resolutions
Accounting books, supporting records, and approved financial statements
Copies of incorporation documents, amendments, licenses, and regulatory filings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,500-5,000 per year, excluding governmental charges, translation, legalization, and sector-specific licensing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000-8,000 per year for a straightforward operating LLC; offshore vessel leasing, foreign currency, related-party, vessel, or multi-jurisdiction activity may increase the fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (base CIT under Law 91/2005; 25% marginal rate applies to net taxable income exceeding EGP 10,000,000; entities registered in an approved Special Economic Zone, including SCZONE, may elect a 15% flat rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law 72/2017: up to 50% CIT reduction for 7 years for strategic projects in Category A zones (effective 11.25%); SCZONE-registered maritime logistics and chartering operators may adopt a 15% SEZ rate; Free Zone establishment status can exempt export-oriented marine charter services from VAT and customs while retaining taxable-segment allocation for domestic Egyptian-source operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Tax Authority Form No. 10 (Corporate Income Tax Declaration); mandatory electronic filing via the ETA portal at tax.gov.eg using the unified tax identification number, e-signature, and attached audited financial statements, trial balance, and supporting schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; quarterly provisional on-account tax installments during the fiscal year (payable in four installments approved by the ETA for the entity's tax card).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year entities must file by April 30. A 1-month extension may be granted upon documented application; all provisional installments must be settled before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unified tax identification number (TIN), commercial register number, and legal form description.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quote the Egyptian LLC's TIN; do not substitute the foreign parent's TIN. The Egyptian LLC is the resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered head office address and actual management location in Egypt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Egyptian office address; foreign directors' addresses must be disclosed in the beneficial owner annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year covered, accounting standards used (IFRS or Egyptian GAAP), and valuation basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calendar year presumed; any non-calendar year requires ETA pre-approval before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: bareboat and time-charter hire from offshore supply vessels, standby rates, mobilization/demobilization fees, and crew/marine-support service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only Egyptian-source charter income. Unpriced diesel pass-through or crew-allowance adjustments will trigger arm's length review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs: crew wages, depreciation of Vessel, hull insurance, harbor dues, dry-dock amortization, flag registration fees, and validated e-invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs allocated to an Egyptian PE must be evidenced by contemporaneous TP allocation keys and a cost contribution arrangement for head-office charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, royalties, and service fees paid to related parties; reconciliation of withholding tax and any DTA relief applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain the recipient's valid Tax Residency Certificate before applying treaty rates; otherwise withhold at statutory rates (20% royalties/services; 20% interest).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: add-back of non-deductible provisions, excessive entertainment, unverified intercompany charges; deduction of statutory tax amortization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the TP benchmarking study and depreciation schedules; material deviations require refiling within 60 days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward set-off: bring forward only losses assessed and accepted by the ETA for the Egyptian chartering business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent losses and pre-incorporation losses are not deductible; only Egyptian-source vessel operations may be offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance tax credits: quarterly provisional payments and withholding credits evidenced by charterers' withholding certificates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify each charterer's TIN and attach the withholding settlement slips; residual credits exceeding the final tax due become refundable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing disclosure: tick declarations for Local File, Master File, and Country-by-Country Report thresholds and identify related foreign counterparties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident groups appointing the Egyptian LLC as a CbCR constituent entity must file the CbCR through the ETA portal within 12 months of the group's reporting period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed fine EGP 500–5,000 plus a 2% monthly surcharge on unpaid tax, capped at 25% of tax. Inaccurate returns: up to 20% penalty on the tax difference. Fraudulent omission or evasion: fine of 100%–300% of evaded tax plus criminal prosecution. E-invoice failures: administrative fines up to EGP 50,000 per missing or invalid e-invoice and suspension of the tax clearance certificate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory final withholding tax on distributions by Egyptian LLCs; the company as withholding agent must remit within 15 days of payment. Treaty-reduced rates commonly 5%–10% subject to holding period, TRC, and beneficial ownership review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1) Obtain the TRC from the residence-state tax authority and complete the Beneficial Owner Declaration. 2) File the DTA relief application with the ETA International Tax Unit at least 5 working days before payment and obtain the ETA approval notice. 3) Apply the treaty withholding rate at source based on that approval. 4) If statutory withholding was already applied, file a refund claim with the ETA, triggering a residency audit and tax clearance review (typical processing 6–12 months).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on gross cross-border royalties for IP, equipment, and technical services: 20%; statutory WHT on interest on debt claims: 20%. Treaty-reduced floors commonly range from 5% to 15% (e.g., UK/Egypt DTA: interest 10%, royalties 12.5%; UAE/Egypt DTA: interest 10%, royalties 10%). Vessel hire payments may be recharacterized as royalty-like rental or shipping income allocation; arm's length charter rates and PE analysis mitigate recharacterization risk.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Annual revenue above EGP 8,000,000 triggers mandatory TP disclosure. Full Local File required where entity revenue exceeds EGP 26,000,000 or related-party transactions exceed EGP 3,000,000 (services) or EGP 6,000,000 (goods). Master File required where consolidated group revenue exceeds EGP 500,000,000. CbCR applies to groups with consolidated revenue above the EUR 750,000,000 equivalent at the filing date exchange rate.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (comparable uncontrolled price) using market charter rates and freight indexes
Transaction net margin method (TNMM) with multiple-year benchmarking
Transactional profit split for integrated offshore service arrangements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt applies no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation, but substantive presence is enforced through (i) GAAR in Article 33 of Law 91/2005, (ii) treaty beneficial-ownership clauses, (iii) the real-seat doctrine and management-and-control test of the Egyptian Commercial Code, and (iv) the MLI Principal Purpose Test for treaty access. The vessel-leasing LLC must demonstrate local contractual authority, physically staffed Egyptian operations, commercial acumen in charter negotiations, vessel registry interests, and audited financials to avoid sham-vehicle recharacterization and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring charter hire, issuing dual invoices to shift Egyptian-flag revenue to an offshore affiliate, maintaining cash-based crew and fuel ledgers, or fabricating vessel operating days.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 150, Law 91/2005: imprisonment of 3–5 years; fine equal to 100%–300% of evaded tax; confiscation of vessel equipment; blacklisting from public tenders; loss of tax clearance certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing directors may be prosecuted as accomplices; personal criminal conviction, travel bans, freezing of personal Egyptian and maritime escrow assets, and restitution of evaded tax with surcharges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: LLC with no Egyptian employment, no physical operations, all management exercised abroad, and use of a nominee beneficial owner solely to obtain treaty or SCZONE advantages; dividend stripping to low-tax conduit states.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization; nullity of treaty benefits; back-taxes assessed with 2% monthly surcharge (cap 25%); evaded-tax fine of up to 20%–40% of recharacterized adjustments; annulment of the investment incentive certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for the disregarded entity's tax debt; administrative travel bans; criminal prosecution where misleading statements were submitted to the ETA International Tax Unit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling cash or bearer instruments above EGP 200,000 in charter, fuel, or crew-wage transactions; failing to file suspicious transaction reports with the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (E-FIU); using unlicensed money transmitters for offshore crew remittance packages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 80/2002 as amended by Law 194/2020: imprisonment 3–7 years and fine EGP 100,000–1,000,000; aggravated or organizational offending up to 15 years' imprisonment; administrative fines and permanent revocation of maritime licenses by E-FIU and the General Authority for Maritime Safety.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability for obstructing E-FIU disclosure; asset freezes ordered by the Money Laundering Combating Unit; D&O insurance indemnification rendered void by willful misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 10 for more than one fiscal year, failure to issue withholding certificates to charterers, or refusing ETA notices for payment of provisional CIT installments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 2% monthly late-payment surcharge capped at 25%; fixed infraction fines EGP 500–5,000; ETA deemed-assessment power; forcible bank garnishment or vessel attachment; refusal of the good tax record certificate; blacklisting from charterer qualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who prefer other creditors over the ETA may face personal recourse for unpaid corporate tax; travel bans applicable where tax arrears exceed EGP 1,000,000; administrative disqualification from maritime licensing boards.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No contemporaneous Local File after breaching the EGP 26,000,000 revenue threshold; intercompany charter rates below arm's length market indexes; phantom sub-chartering through conduit jurisdictions without benchmarking; non-filing of CbCR after group threshold is crossed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustment with a 20% penalty on the adjustment amount; rejection of the taxpayer's own margin data; administrative fines for missing Local File or CbCR from EGP 100,000 up to EGP 1,000,000; criminal penalties if the TP documentation is forged.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De facto directors signing false benchmarking or margin certificates face joint and several liability for the additional tax and surcharges; willful misrepresentation attracts criminal prosecution and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an offshore supply vessel under a foreign flag without the required Egyptian maritime authorization, breaching Suez Canal Authority transit restrictions, or undertaking cabotage prohibited by Egyptian Maritime Law; omission of compulsory maritime safety insurance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vessel arrest and detention; suspension or cancellation of the offshore charter license; fine up to double the unlawful charter hire; suspension of the offshore operations permit under Law 1/1996 (Egyptian Maritime Law) and Law 12/1998.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal prosecution for willful maritime safety breaches; admiralty court may impose travel bans and freeze Egyptian assets; director license revocation; liability overrides any corporate indemnity.
